notes.decision: Translated tentatively as 'the Awakening' from root ⲧⲱⲛ 'rise.' The form is unattested elsewhere in this corpus and may be a corruption or scribal variant. Possible alternatives: a hapax technical term, or scribal variant for ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ ('the Calling'); but the latter would be redundant with the explicit ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ later in the same line. Provisionally read as a topic-marker referring to the awakening/raising-up that frames the entire kephalaion's letter-typology.
Lyc. ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' (= glossary ⲡⲁⲝⲉ); the final -ϩ is the regular Lyc. orthographic substitute for -ϥ (3sg.m. suffix). Standard discourse-introducer.
'As for / concerning' — Lyc. topic-marker already attested in glossary (page 173 context).
'She established them' — feminine 3sg subject (the letter, ⲉⲡⲓⲥⲧⲟⲗⲏ, is feminine in Greek/Coptic) + ⲥⲙⲛⲧ 'establish, set' + 3pl object. The letter establishes its readers in the Calling.
Probably qualitative-passive of ⲥϩⲁⲓ 'write,' rendered 'stands written / is decreed.' The ⲛⲏⲩⲧ ending may be a Lyc. plural-passive or assimilated form. Confidence moderate.

Apparently truncated verb form before lacuna. Possibly ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲥⲧⲁ[ϩⲟⲩ] 'so that they set them up' (causative ⲧⲁϩⲟ) or ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲥⲧⲁ[ⲩⲟ] 'that she utter forth.' Translated provisionally with the directional reflex 'returned' from ⲥⲧⲟ 'turn back', appropriate to the cosmic-correspondence imagery (the Answer-letter as return-message).
The supralinear ⲁ̄ at line-start likely functions as the perfect prefix or topicalization marker for the new clause. Translated by zero (continuing predication on 'the Living Spirit').

'The Mind of Light' = ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ in glossary. Standard Manichaean technical term — the fourth drawer-upward, here the heavenly source of the third 'letter' (the apocalypses and Wisdom sent to the Church).
'Was foremost / did first.' Lyc. perfect ⲁϩ-ⲣ̄- + ⲱⲁⲣⲡⲧ qualitative ('first'). Construction parallels ϯⲍⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲧⲉ 'do first' in glossary.

Obscure noun. Most plausible reading: Lyc. orthographic variant of ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲟⲗⲏ (= ⲉⲡⲓⲥⲧⲟⲗⲏ 'letter') with ⲝ for ⲥⲧ — fitting the kephalaion's pervasive letter-typology and the parallel ϩⲱϩ ⲁⲛ ⲧⲉ ('too is it') in line 30. Alternative: from ⲥⲧⲟ 'turn back, return' — 'this returning'. Translated tentatively 'this {term}' to flag uncertainty; the fourth letter completes the four-letter scheme (Calling/Answer/Mind-of-Light/X), most likely the Church's responsive letter.

'This offspring of light' (or 'gift of light' if from ⲙⲏⲥⲉ in alternative sense). The verb ϣⲁⲩⲭⲡⲧⲁⲥ 'they take her forth' indicates feminine antecedent: the offspring is what the Church gives forth as her 'letter' to the higher powers.
'Her Father' — feminine possessive referring to the Church (ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ); the Father here is the heavenly source (Christ Beloved or the Greatness) who exhorts the Church.
'In this manner' — already in glossary as ⲡⲓⲣⲏⲧⲉ. Standard discourse formulation in Kephalaia.
